NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to introduce a hydrophobic silica nanoparticle network into the ethylene-vinyl alcohol (EVOH) layer during extrusion to physically block moisture ingress and reduce polymer chain mobility. Standard practice uses neat EVOH or conventional moisture scavengers; this mitigation departs by creating a tortuous path for water molecules and physically restricting chain plasticization through a nanostructured filler network that does not rely on chemical reaction. The closest existing practice is polymer nanocomposites in non-food applications (e.g., automotive gas tanks), but this differs by using food-grade silica at low loading to maintain optical clarity and compliance while directly addressing the humidity-driven plasticization mechanism in EVOH.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's first law of diffusion: J = -D·(Δc/Δx), where J is flux, D is diffusivity, and Δc/Δx is concentration gradient. Silica nanoparticles reduce D by two mechanisms: (1) increasing tortuosity (reducing Δx by ~30% per vol% loading), and (2) restricting chain mobility (lowering D by ~20% per vol% loading via free volume reduction). At 3 vol% silica, D decreases by ~50%, reducing J below the 0.5 g/m2/day threshold at 65% RH.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- Replace standard EVOH resin with food-grade silica masterbatch (3 wt% loading in EVOH) (b)
- Adjust extrusion screw speed by 5% to compensate for increased melt viscosity (c)
- Implement inline near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy to verify silica dispersion uniformity (a)
- Modify cooling roll temperature profile from 20°C to 15°C to optimize crystallinity (c)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
| Standard Practice Items | Intervention Items | Burden Change |
|------------------------|---------------------|---------------|
| Neat EVOH resin | Silica masterbatch (b) | Same material class, same procurement burden |
| Standard extrusion parameters | Modified screw speed (c) | No new equipment, parameter adjustment |
| Standard QC sampling | Inline NIR monitoring (a) | Existing instrument repurposed |
| Standard cooling profile | Modified cooling (c) | No new hardware, parameter change |
Total burden: Same class (material, equipment, procedure) with no new infrastructure.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Package identical food products in both standard and modified films; store at 25°C/65% RH for 18 months. Measure water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) monthly using ASTM E96 gravimetric cups.
Instruments: Analytical balance (±0.1 mg), environmental chamber.
Pass/fail: Modified film maintains WVTR <0.5 g/m2/day at all time points; standard film exceeds threshold by month 6.
Duration: 18 months with monthly measurements.
Kill criterion: If modified film exceeds 0.5 g/m2/day at any point, the intervention fails.

BILL_UNTAGGED: - Burden: Same material class (polymer resin), same equipment class (extrusion line), same
- Protocol: Accelerated aging at 40°C/80% RH for 6 weeks (equivalent to 18 months at 25°C/
- Pass/fail: WVTR ≤0.5 g/m²/day at test end.
- Kill criterion: WVTR >0.6 g/m²/day at any point (20% above constraint).
